In all fairness, US Treasury Secretary Bessent was already behind the 8-ball before he started.

The US is now running $2+ trillion deficits, spending over $1.2 trillion on annual interest expense, and fighting 60 consecutive months of 2%+ inflation.

On top of this, oil prices have nearly doubled since the Iran War began, inflation expectations are surging, and the Fed went from rate cuts to discussing rate hikes.

Taming the surge in yields is nearly impossible over the long-term, even for the US Treasury itself, without a structural shift in several of these fundamental drivers.

Simply put, "free money" is only "free" for so long, and the world cannot handle $100+ oil prices on top of compounding inflation.

As an investor, the only thing you can do is position yourself accordingly.

That's exactly what we are doing.

You can't make this up.

The US Treasury just announced it is tripling long-term buybacks to $6 billion and yields STILL rallied on the news.

That means the US Treasury went from doubling, to "at least doubling," to tripling long-term bond buybacks and yields are still rising.

This puts the 10Y Note Yield above 4.85% for the first time since November 2023, up +15 basis points from pre-announcement levels.

The bond market is quite literally fighting the US Treasury as the Iran War continues, with the 10Y Note Yield nearing a +100 basis point move since the war began.

Without an end to the Iran War, we are on track to see the 10Y Note Yield above 5.00% by next week.

The most interesting chart from my investigation into Bitcoin's AI divide wasn't about Bitcoin at all.

AI engineers have been significantly more convicted than AI investors for most of this year.

This is in stark contrast to summer of 2024 (where Nvidia destroyed earnings expectations while Google's AI launch backfired).

But we're seeing the opposite now.

AI engineers (people consistently building cool stuff with AI) have been persistently higher conviction than people investing in the buildout... and that gap is now widening.

It makes sense.

AI stocks have been relatively choppy YTD, but at the same time, the people building with these things are seeing insane productivity improvements month over month.

Hard to call the technology overhyped when it keeps exceeding the expectations of the people using it every day.

BREAKING: China’s central bank officially bought +20 tonnes of gold in August, matching its largest monthly purchase since October 2023.

This follows +20 tonnes and +15 tonnes acquired in July and June, respectively, and marks its 22nd consecutive monthly gold purchase.

So far in 2026, China has officially added +80 tonnes to its gold reserves, lifting total holdings to a record 2,387 tonnes.

By comparison, in full-year 2025, China increased its official gold reserves by a total of +29 tonnes.

In troy ounces, China added ~650,000 ounces to its reserves last month, taking its total holdings to a record 76.73 million ounces.

China continues to stockpile gold at a historic pace.

RT @CarsonResearch: Odds of a Fed hike on September 16 are hovering near 60%. Our base case is still no hike this year. But if we are wrong…

The AI Revolution is fueling a record financing boom in the US:

US high-grade corporate bond issuance is expected to surge to ~$215 billion in September, the largest September issuance on record.

This is set to surpass the previous September high of ~$205 billion, posted in 2025.

The current estimate is also more than triple the ~$70 billion issued in September 2022.

This follows $145.2 billion of US high-grade bonds issued in August, the highest August total on record, as AI-related data center buildouts continue to fuel corporate borrowing.

US companies have already borrowed more than $410 billion so far in 2026, specifically to fund data centers and other AI-related investments.

Meanwhile, retail investors have purchased more investment-grade bonds this year than in any full year in data going back to 2010.

The AI boom is driving a record corporate borrowing spree.

Rinse the Damn Tub

I’ve traded gold for fifty years,
Through bull runs, busts and pain.
I’ve bought the lows and sold the highs,
Then bought the highs again.

I’ve studied charts and measured moves,
Drawn lines both thick and thin.
I’ve risked a fortune on a trade
And sometimes even win.

I’ve battled markets night and day,
Made money, lost it too.
I’ve stared down fear and margin calls
And somehow muddled through.

I’ve learned that gold is fickle stuff.
It sparkles, then it bites.
It makes a genius out of fools
And fools of us some nights.

But after all these years of gold,
One lesson tops the list.
It wasn’t learned from charts or books,
And cannot be dismissed.

You may have gold inside your vault.
You may have millions more.
You may have nailed the greatest trade
That markets ever saw.

You may be king of commodities,
A legend in your mind.
But marriage has a marking system
Of quite a different kind.

For when the trading day is done,
There’s one immutable truth:

Your wife does not give a damn about gold.
Just rinse the damn tub.

Gold-mining margins are surging well ahead of gold prices:

Average all-in sustaining cost (AISC) margins surged +134% YoY in Q1 2026, to a record $3,076 per ounce.

AISC margin is the amount miners earn per ounce of gold after covering the costs of sustaining their mining operations.

This is far above the +70% YoY increase in gold prices over the same period.

Furthermore, AISC margins among the 10% of gold miners with the highest production costs rose +32% QoQ, to $2,363 per ounce.

Since March 2024, global miner AISC margins have more than tripled, while gold prices have roughly doubled over the same period.

Gold miners are realizing massive profits.
